ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: at the bottom of the figure are two adjacent unit squares, side by side left and right; above there is one unit square, centered above the common vertical side of the two bottom squares. The whole figure is symmetric about the middle vertical line; the diagonal and vertical line inside the upper square are only auxiliary lines and do not change the outer boundary. Then reason: establish a coordinate system according to the figure, let the bottom edges of the two bottom unit squares lie on y=0, and let the common vertical side be x=0. Then the two bottom outside bottom corners are (-1,0) and (1,0), and the two top corners of the upper square are (-1/2,2) and (1/2,2). Since the figure is symmetric about the y-axis, the center of the smallest enclosing circle is also on the y-axis, set as (0,c). The circle radius must at least cover the bottom outside corners and the upper top corners. The squared distance to a bottom outside corner is 1+c^2; the squared distance to an upper top corner is (1/2)^2+(2-c)^2. In order to make the maximum distance minimal, set the two equal: 1+c^2 = 1/4+(2-c)^2. Expanding gives 1+c^2 = 1/4+4-4c+c^2, so 1 = 17/4-4c, solving gives c=13/16. Therefore the radius r satisfies r^2=1+c^2=1+169/256=425/256=25·17/256, so r=5√17/16.

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates from the diagram. Read the figure as two adjacent unit squares on the bottom and one unit square centered above their common vertical boundary, so the outer extreme vertices can be taken as bottom corners (-1,0), (1,0) and top corners (-1/2,2), (1/2,2). By symmetry, the smallest enclosing circle has its center on the vertical axis, say (0,c). The radius must be at least the distance to the bottom outer corners and to the top outer corners. Minimize the maximum of these two distances by equating them: 1+c^2 = (1/2)^2+(2-c)^2. Solve c=13/16, then compute r = sqrt(1+c^2)=sqrt(1+169/256)=5sqrt(17)/16.

圆半径至少要覆盖底部外角和上方顶角。到底部外角的距离平方为 1+c^2；到上方顶角的距离平方为 (1/2)^2+(2-c)^2。为了使最大距离最小，令两者相等：
1+c^2 = 1/4+(2-c)^2。
展开得 1+c^2 = 1/4+4-4c+c^2，所以 1 = 17/4-4c，解得 c=13/16。

因此半径 r 满足 r^2=1+c^2=1+169/256=425/256=25·17/256，所以 r=5√17/16。
